name: Killing Floor
description: Killing Floor (the 2009 original, Unreal Engine 2) dedicated server: Steam app 215360, native Linux 32-bit binary (System/ucc-bin), anonymous SteamCMD login. All settings are written to System/KillingFloor.ini on every start, seeded from the game's Default.ini the first time. The classic WebAdmin runs on an internal port and is reachable only through the panel (WebAdmin tab; HTTP basic auth with the admin name and password). Steam Workshop: items are downloaded with SteamCMD (workshop app 1250) and their files are copied into System/. Limitation: a downloaded item is NOT activated automatically; mutators and server packages still have to be enabled (use 'Extra URL options' such as ?Mutator=Package.Class, or edit System/KillingFloor.ini with the Files tab), and the item's sounds/textures/animations may need to be moved to the matching game folders by hand. The Steam query port is always the game port + 1, which the panel allocates and publishes automatically so the server can be listed in the Steam server browser.

variables.label: Server name
variables.description: Name shown in the server browser (Engine.GameReplicationInfo ServerName).

variables.label: Message of the day
variables.description: Message shown to joining players (MessageOfTheDay). May be empty.

variables.label: Game password
variables.description: Password players must enter to join. Leave empty for a public server.

variables.label: Admin name
variables.description: Administrator name (GameReplicationInfo AdminName). It is also the user name the panel sends to the WebAdmin. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore only.

variables.label: Admin password
variables.description: Admin password for the in-game admin login and the WebAdmin. Leave empty to have one generated when the server is created (12 characters); managers can read and regenerate it in Settings. 6 to 16 characters, no spaces.

variables.label: Admin e-mail
variables.description: Contact e-mail shown in the server info (AdminEmail). May be empty.

variables.label: Enable WebAdmin
variables.description: Enables the built-in web administration (UWeb.WebServer). It is not published to the internet: it is only reachable through the panel's WebAdmin tab.

variables.label: Starting map
variables.description: Map the server starts on, without extension, for example KF-BioticsLab, KF-Farm, KF-Manor, KF-WestLondon. Must exist in the Maps folder.

variables.label: Difficulty
variables.description: GameDifficulty: Beginner 1, Normal 2, Hard 4, Suicidal 5, Hell on Earth 7.

variables.label: Game length
variables.description: KFGameLength: Short 4 waves, Medium 7 waves, Long 10 waves. 'Custom' uses the wave counts configured in the ini.

variables.label: Max players
variables.description: Maximum number of players (Engine.GameInfo MaxPlayers and the MaxPlayers URL option). The game is designed for 6; more players need a capable CPU and the server mod ecosystem.

variables.label: Friendly fire scale
variables.description: FriendlyFireScale from 0.0 (off) to 1.0 (full damage to teammates).

variables.label: Seasonal specimens
variables.description: SpecialEventType: which seasonal zed set to use.

variables.label: VAC secured
variables.description: Start the server with Valve Anti-Cheat (VACSecured=true). Disable it to allow clients with mods that VAC would block.

variables.label: Fast download URL
variables.description: HTTP redirect server URL for custom content (IpDrv.HTTPDownload RedirectToURL), starting with http:// or https://. Empty disables fast download.

variables.label: Extra URL options
variables.description: Advanced. Extra options appended to the map URL, WITHOUT a leading question mark; separate several with a question mark, for example Mutator=Package.Class?FriendlyFireScale=0.5. Leave empty if unsure. A wrong value can prevent the server from starting.

scripts.postInstall: if [ ! -f System/KillingFloor.ini ] && [ -f System/Default.ini ]; then cp System/Default.ini System/KillingFloor.ini; fi
scripts.preStart: for f in steamclient.so libtier0_s.so libvstdlib_s.so; do if [ -f /opt/steamcmd/linux32/$f ]; then cp -f /opt/steamcmd/linux32/$f System/$f; fi; done; true
